why_trail.why: Read global-crew/global-everyone doctrine, CREW_CONTEXT.md (py interpreter, utf-8/newline writes, no hand-editing checklists), handoff is complete (task/intent/scope/exclusions/evidence/stop conditions/return format all present), cli.py's _build/HANDLERS, gauge_writer_hook.py's fail-open precedent, and MapTreeFreshnessTests (byte/text-normalized comparison against a fresh build).

build.py created with build(root, *, artifacts=None, out=None) seam wrapping extract.run/render.run; cli._build now delegates to it (one-line change, no other cli.py edit). BuildSeamTests.test_cli_build_and_library_build_are_byte_identical proves the CLI subprocess path and the direct build() call produce byte-identical INDEX.md/ids.jsonl for this repo's own tree.

precommit.run_precommit() implements the index-snapshot mechanism end to end (worktree prune, write-tree/commit-tree/worktree add via tempfile.mkdtemp, build() against the ephemeral worktree, plain-file-I/O copy-back diffed against 'git show :path', git add of only changed paths, worktree remove in a finally). Verified manually against a real scratch repo (fresh/no-op, then a staged source edit correctly triggering rebuild) before encoding as tests. PrecommitCoreTests (fresh/no-op, stale/rebuild-exact-two-paths, cleanup) all pass.

PartialCommitTests proves the mechanism snapshots the git INDEX, not the working tree, on all three commit shapes: pathspec-restricted (git add pkg/a.py only, b.py's edit stays out of the built map, verified via root INDEX.md's per-module entity counts since only INDEX.md/ids.jsonl survive copy-back), hunk-restricted (a hand-split git apply --cached patch stages exactly one of two well-separated hunks, and only that hunk's function raises the entity count), and unrelated-dirty-file audit (a third tracked file dirty staged or unstaged throughout never appears in the mechanism's OWN newly-staged set, computed as a before/after diff of git diff --cached --name-only).

Concurrent-invocation, forced-timeout, and forced-exception tests all pass (verified 10 consecutive direct runs plus this advance); the Honest-Null escape hatch was not needed. A genuine hazard WAS found and fixed along the way: the first concurrent-invocation draft used Python threading against ONE shared worktree path, which hit two unrelated hazards real concurrent git commits never would -- extract.py's module-level TABLES/ROOT globals cross-talking across threads in one interpreter, and two processes fighting over one shared index.lock on 'git write-tree' for the SAME worktree. Real concurrent commits are separate OS processes on SEPARATE sibling worktrees, each with its own per-worktree index since git 2.5 -- so the test now uses two real subprocesses against two sibling worktrees of one repo, the actual shape the mechanism must be safe under. Forced-timeout targets exactly one subprocess call (git write-tree) to hang for the full 10s budget before raising TimeoutExpired, proving fail-open bounds it near 10s, well under the ~15s ceiling. Forced-exception fails a call made AFTER the ephemeral worktree exists (during copy-back), proving cleanup fires mid-mechanism, leaving the real repo's status and worktree list untouched.

scripts/hooks/code_map_precommit.py resolves repo_root dynamically via git rev-parse --show-toplevel from cwd, then dynamically imports THAT resolved repo's own scripts/code_map/precommit.py (sys.path.insert + importlib.import_module, never a package the process happened to have cached) and calls its already-fail-open main(). The shim's own try/except covers exactly the layer main() cannot: resolving which repo it's even in, and importing a module that may not exist there at all. ShimTests: real-subprocess stage/no-op pass, and worktree-run-time-resolution confirms exit 0 with a 'fail-open' stderr line when invoked from a worktree checked out before scripts/code_map/precommit.py existed (the ImportError path).

Full precommit + protected freshness suite green (161 passed, 65 subtests; tests/test_code_map.py has zero byte diff). Wiring grep counts recorded: build() has exactly 2 real call sites (cli._build's refactor, precommit.py's own call); code_map_precommit/scripts.code_map.precommit has exactly 1 real (non-docstring, non-test-file) reference -- the shim's own dynamic import -- matching the handoff's expectation that gate 2's installer is what gives the shim a real caller. Timing re-measured end to end (write-tree/commit-tree/worktree add/build/copy-back/remove) against a local clone carrying this repo's real corpus (175 modules): 3.25-3.77s no-op runs, confirming the mechanism stays fast including worktree materialization, not just the previously-measured 2.9s build-only baseline. IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.md written to .agent-work/w2-reindex/crew-handoffs/g1-implement-implementer-result.md with Return status: complete.
